To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a linear-time algorithm for the computation all $$\rho$$ρ-avoided (of any length, not necessarily k) words in a sequence of n elements over a fixed-sized (integer) alphabet, and we provide a combinatorial upper bound for the length of the longest avoided word.

we present a fast and efficient algorithm for the computation, in a given sequence, of all avoided words, of any length, and that we present combinatorial and experimental results with regards to the number and length of these words.

we present a linear-time algorithm that finds all $$\rho$$ρ-avoided k-words in a given sequence, and that we present an asymptotically tight upper bound for the expected length of longest $$\rho$$rho-avoided word.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic analysis of the deviation of the observed frequencies of words in biological sequences.
the efficient and systematic search for avoided and absent words in a given sequence.
the efficient computation of avoided words in a given sequence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the algorithm presented in this article is a very efficient and useful tool in biological sequence analysis, and that the results obtained in this article are of interest for both biological sequence analysis and combinatorial analysis.
the systematic search for avoided and absent words in a sequence is a useful and efficient tool for biological sequence analysis, in particular in DNA linguistic analysis and motif discovery.

we present an efficient, time and memory saving algorithm for the search for avoided words in a given sequence and we provide a thorough theoretical background to support the practical applicability of our algorithm.

we provide a systematic and efficient way for the computation of words that are avoided and absent in a given sequence.
our algorithm can be used to find all words that are absent or avoided, in a given sequence.

the systematic search for avoided and absent words is a useful tool in DNA linguistic analysis.
